See AMC.1701 and AMC.1701 (e)
(a) The UAV control station (UCS) of a UAV System is the facility or device from which the UAV is remotely controlled. A UAV System may be comprised of more than one UCS.
(b) The design of a UCS must facilitate the command and control of the UAV by the UAV crew for safe operations as agreed by the Certifying Authority.
(c) When the UCS is to be used on a moving platform, the Certifying Authority may require establishing a Special Condition.
(d) It must be shown using the UAV system safety analysis according to USAR.1309 that all identified hazards within the UCS have been reduced to a level consistent with safe operation of the system.
(e) The UAV control station must be designed and its performance established by test for operation over the complete target environment as determined by an Environmental Life Cycle analysis. This analysis shall take into account the full range of operational and non-operational (storage, transportation, etc) environments.

See AMC.U1701 and AMC.U1701 (e)
(a) The UAS control station (UCS) of a UAS is the facility or device from which the UA is remotely controlled. A UAS may be comprised of more than one UCS.
(b) The design of a UCS must facilitate the command and control of the UA by the UAS crew for safe operations as agreed with the Certifying Authority.
(c) When the UCS is to be used on a moving platform, the Certifying Authority may require establishing a Special Condition.
(d) It must be shown using the UAS System Safety Assessment (SSA) according to USAR.1309 that all identified hazards within the UCS have been reduced to a level consistent with safe operation of the system.
(e) The UAS control station must be designed and its performance established by test for operation over the complete target environment as determined by an Environmental Life Cycle analysis. This analysis shall take into account the full range of operational and non-operational (storage, transportation, etc.) environments.
(f) Some of the following sub-part 1 requirements related to data and markings to be displayed may not apply if the Applicant shows that specific design features (such as closed loop flight control with adequate stability characteristics and flight envelope protection) make the display or the marking of a specific parameter unnecessary as agreed with the Certifying Authority.
